_about: Behaviour and animation numbers for the Den Ledger hero (Carolina Dog, ~15-20 kg, ~45-50 cm at the withers). Each entry: value, unit, source (title + URL), confidence (high/medium/low/estimate), notes. 'MANN-derived' means Firefly measured it from the MANN dog mocap (see REPORT.md; source data is research/education-only, numbers here are our own measurements). 'estimate' means no published number was found and the value is a design guess for the game. Compiled 2026-10-06 by Firefly.

gait.walk.unit: m/s, s, fraction of stride, fraction of stride, cm peak-to-peak
gait.walk.source: MANN-derived (50 strides). Mode-Adaptive Neural Networks for Quadruped Motion Control, Zhang, Starke, Komura, Saito 2018, https://github.com/sebastianstarke/AI4Animation
gait.walk.confidence: high for this dog; the walk is slow (0.64 m/s), a brisk dog walk is ~1 m/s
gait.walk.notes: Lateral-sequence walk: LH, LF, RH, RF. Stride frequency ~1.1 Hz.

gait.trot.unit: m/s, s, fraction, fraction, cm peak-to-peak
gait.trot.confidence: medium (only 8 clean trot strides in the mirrored clips)
gait.trot.notes: Diagonal pairs (LH+RF, RH+LF) land together. Two bobs per stride (2 Hz stride -> 4 Hz bob). Labradors trot at ~2.3 m/s in the literature.

gait.pace.source: MANN-derived (114 strides). AI4Animation SIGGRAPH 2018 ReadMe notes 'Default locomotion is pace'
gait.pace.notes: Same-side legs move together; tired or long-legged dogs often pace at slow speed. Not usually what we want for the hero, but this is the best-sampled gait in the data.

gait.gallop_rotary.source: MANN-derived (16 strides, one lead). AI4Animation SIGGRAPH 2018
gait.gallop_rotary.confidence: medium (slow gallop / fast canter; only one lead kept)
gait.gallop_rotary.notes: Sequence RH -> LH -> LF -> RF: rotary gallop (hind lead L, fore lead R). Mirror for the other lead.

gait.joint_rom_literature_walk.source: Kinematic motion analysis of the joints of the forelimbs and hind limbs of dogs during walking exercise regimens, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/44900733
gait.joint_rom_literature_walk.confidence: medium (seen via search summary, not the full paper)
gait.joint_rom_literature_walk.notes: MANN-derived walk ROM: shoulder 25, elbow 39, carpus 75, hip 42, stifle 29, hock 18. Our hock ROM is low; MANN dog walked slowly.

gait.carpus_rom_literature.source: Kinematics of healthy American Pit Bull Terrier dogs, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11927105
gait.carpus_rom_literature.notes: MANN-derived trot carpus ROM 124 deg, agrees.

tail.wag_frequency_relaxed.unit: Hz (full left-right-left cycles per second), 10-90th percentile range
tail.wag_frequency_relaxed.source: MANN-derived: 33 wag bouts while the dog stood still (121 bouts in total, all ~1.4 Hz)
tail.wag_frequency_relaxed.confidence: medium (one dog, mocap context, probably mild/relaxed wagging)
tail.wag_frequency_relaxed.notes: Use as the slow friendly wag. Excited wags are faster: see tail.wag_frequency_range.

tail.wag_amplitude_relaxed.unit: degrees peak-to-peak, whole tail (base-to-tip chord), 10-90th percentile
tail.wag_amplitude_relaxed.notes: Bouts last a median 4.8 s while standing (IQR ~4-9 s). Tail held ~40-50 deg below caudal horizontal during these bouts.

tail.wag_frequency_range.source: Does the tail show when the nose knows? (Royal Society Open Science 2025) https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12344452/ ; Left-right asymmetry and attractor-like dynamics of dog's tail wagging during dog-human interactions (iScience 2022) https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9356099/
tail.wag_frequency_range.confidence: medium (1-4 Hz peak frequency and 5 Hz upper bound seen in summaries; exact per-study numbers not read)
tail.wag_frequency_range.notes: A wag is usually counted from >= 20 deg peak-to-peak. Asymmetry: bigger swings to the dog's right for positive stimuli (owner), to the left for negative/withdrawal (Quaranta et al. 2007, Current Biology https://www.cell.com/current-biology/fulltext/S0960-9822(07)00949-9).

tail.wag_min_amplitude_definition.source: Automated Depth Sensing-Based Computer Vision for Dog Tail Wagging Interpretation, https://dl.acm.org/doi/fullHtml/10.1145/3702336.3702340

tail.carriage_standing_still.unit: degrees elevation of the whole tail vs. caudal horizontal (negative = below)
tail.carriage_standing_still.source: MANN-derived (19 standing-still windows); trot ~-25, rotary gallop ~-10 to 0
tail.carriage_standing_still.confidence: medium for that dog; NOT breed-typical for a Carolina Dog
tail.carriage_standing_still.notes: Carolina Dog: tail usually carried low-to-level when relaxed, raised in a fish-hook curve when alert or excited (breed standards). Treat as estimate for the hero.

breathing.rest_awake.source: VCA Hospitals, Home Breathing Rate Evaluation, https://vcahospitals.com/know-your-pet/home-breathing-rate-evaluation ; FirstVet, How to Measure Resting Respiratory Rates in Dogs, https://firstvet.com/us/articles/how-to-measure-resting-respiratory-rates-in-dogs
breathing.rest_awake.notes: Use ~20/min for the idle chest rise (3 s cycle).

breathing.sleeping.source: Monitoring Your Dog's Sleeping Respiratory Rate (veterinary chart), https://evolutionvet.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Dog-Chart-Final-1.pdf ; Resting respiratory rates for monitoring (vetcardiologist), http://www.vetcardiologist.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/08/Resting-Resp-Rate.7.4.141.pdf
breathing.sleeping.notes: Use ~12-15/min asleep (4-5 s cycle), slow and deep.

breathing.panting.source: Crawford EC, Mechanical aspects of panting in dogs, J Appl Physiol 1962, https://journals.physiology.org/doi/abs/10.1152/jappl.1962.17.2.249 (5.33 +/- 0.7 Hz); Pulmonary gas exchange in panting dogs, https://journals.physiology.org/doi/abs/10.1152/jappl.1989.66.3.1258 (313 +/- 19 /min)
breathing.panting.notes: Dogs pant at the chest-lung resonant frequency. 5 Hz is very fast on screen: for animation, a visible tongue/jaw pump at ~3-5 Hz with small amplitude reads well. Light exercise panting is slower and irregular (estimate 2-3 Hz).

eyes.blink_rate.source: Spontaneous blink rates of domestic dogs: a preliminary report, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/251690906_Spontaneous_blink_rates_of_domestic_dogs_a_preliminary_report
eyes.blink_rate.notes: Carolina Dog is mesocephalic: ~10/min, i.e. random interval ~3-9 s. A more recent study found 6.5 +/- 3.8 /min. Blinks are also social signals (dogs blink back at blinking dogs: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11836432/).

body.wet_dog_shake_frequency.source: Dickerson, Mills, Hu, Wet mammals shake at tuned frequencies to dry, J R Soc Interface 2012, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3481573 ; https://hoogle.gatech.edu/Publications/Hu12-dog.pdf
body.wet_dog_shake_frequency.notes: For a 15-20 kg Carolina Dog use ~4.8-5 Hz (between Labrador and Chihuahua).

body.wet_dog_shake_amplitude.unit: degrees of roll about the body axis
body.wet_dog_shake_amplitude.source: Science Looks at Why and How Wet Dogs Shake (Psychology Today, on Dickerson et al.), https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/canine-corner/201209/science-looks-why-and-how-wet-dogs-shake
body.wet_dog_shake_amplitude.notes: Shake starts at the head and travels to the tail (wave). Head twists most.

body.wet_dog_shake_duration.unit: seconds to shed ~70% of the water
body.wet_dog_shake_duration.source: Science Looks at Why and How Wet Dogs Shake, https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/canine-corner/201209/science-looks-why-and-how-wet-dogs-shake
body.wet_dog_shake_duration.notes: A single visible shake bout in a game is better at ~1-1.5 s (5-7 oscillations), head first then body then tail (estimate).

nose.sniff_frequency.source: Craven, Paterson, Settles 2010, The fluid dynamics of canine olfaction, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20007171/ ; The Secret of a Dog's Sniffer (Science), https://www.science.org/content/article/secret-dogs-sniffer
nose.sniff_frequency.notes: Same ~5 Hz across dog sizes. Long sniff bouts come in bursts at 0.5-1.5 Hz. Animate as tiny nostril/head pulses at 5 Hz, grouped in bursts.

jaw.max_gape_angle.source: Thomson, Hetzel, Snyder, Gape Angle in Asymptomatic Dogs with Normal Occlusion, J Vet Dent 2021, https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/08987564211012487
jaw.max_gape_angle.notes: Use as the yawn peak. Interincisal opening 107 +/- 30 mm for all dogs, 134 +/- 19 mm for >25 kg (Vertical Mandibular Range of Motion in Anesthetized Dogs and Cats, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4923261/). Panting gape is much smaller (estimate 10-20 deg).

jaw.yawn_duration.source: Search summary of contagious-yawning studies in dogs (no primary paper read); see Romero et al. 2013 and Madsen and Persson 2013 via https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/article/130808-yawning-dogs-contagious-animals-empathy-science
jaw.yawn_duration.notes: Stress yawns are longer and more intense than sleepy yawns. Suggest 1.5-3 s with a ~0.5 s hold at full gape, tongue curling, eyes squinting (estimate).

social.play_bow_duration.source: Byosiere, Espinosa, Smuts 2016, Investigating the function of play bows in adult pet dogs, https://bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/about.illinoisstate.edu/dist/6/45/files/2019/10/byosiere-epinosa-smuts-2016-invest-funct-of-play-bows-in-adult-pet-dogs.pdf
social.play_bow_duration.notes: Starts when the front legs begin to bend, ends when elbows straighten again, the dog lies down, or the rear is no longer higher than the front. Pose: elbows/forearms on the ground, rear high, tail up/wagging (descriptive).

head.tilt.source: No angle found. Sommese et al. 2021, An exploratory analysis of head-tilting in dogs, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355649486_An_exploratory_analysis_of_head-tilting_in_dogs
head.tilt.confidence: estimate for the angle; high for the behaviour facts
head.tilt.notes: Each dog tilts to the same side consistently. Word-learner dogs tilted in 43% of trials vs 2% for typical dogs, i.e. tilt is a rare 'processing a familiar word' signal, not a constant idle.

value.EAD104: ears rotator (turned outward/sideways) [from memory, not confirmed in this search]

ears.action_units.source: DogFACS manual (Waller et al.), as used in: Evaluating the accuracy of facial expressions as emotion indicators across contexts in dogs, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353647503 ; Behavioural Analysis of Dogs' Response to Threatening and Neutral Conspecific Video Stimuli, https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/13/16/9254
ears.action_units.notes: EAD101 held longer in threatening contexts (alert/forward); EAD103 with fear/stress; flattened ears can also be a soft greeting when the body is loose.

relaxed.note: upright but loose, slightly out to the side

fearful.note: pinned back and down flat to the skull (EAD103 + EAD105)

ears_back_greeting.note: back and soft, with squinty eyes and loose body

listening.note: one ear at a time swivels 30-60 deg towards a sound, then returns

ears.pose_by_mood.unit: degrees relative to the neutral upright ear in side view (negative = back/down)
ears.pose_by_mood.source: estimate (Firefly) from DogFACS descriptors and behaviour guides, e.g. Hill's Guide to Dog Ear Position, https://www.hillspet.com/dog-care/behavior-appearance/dog-ear-language-and-positions
ears.pose_by_mood.notes: No published ear angles found. Carolina Dog ears are large and erect, so the swing reads strongly.

posture.transition_durations.unit: seconds (median), time for 5% to 95% of the height change; n = 12, 15, 7, 8, 3, 3
posture.transition_durations.source: MANN-derived (stand/sit/lie detected from hip and shoulder heights)
posture.transition_durations.notes: Lying down is slow and often goes via a sit or a front-end-first fold (variable 1-4 s); getting up is quick (~0.6 s).

posture.heights.unit: m (joint-centre heights of the MANN skeleton, not anatomical withers)
posture.heights.notes: Sitting keeps the front ~87% as high as standing. Scale by the hero's height.
